key_insight: QuasiStim enables exact, scalable simulation of non-Pauli noise in fault-tolerant quantum circuits by combining circuit-level merging of equivalent noise sites with trajectory reuse during sampling.
engineering_relevance: This gives quantum engineers a practical alternative to Pauli-twirled approximations when evaluating real hardware noise, decoder performance, and QEC circuit schedules.
method: QuasiFold merges equivalent non-Pauli noise locations to reduce sampling overhead.
DeltaFrame reuses predicted references to sample stabilizer trajectories without resimulating the full tableau each shot.
Targets realistic noise such as coherent control errors and thermal relaxation in large QEC circuits.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports over 100× shot reduction on bivariate-bicycle codes and 166×–1331× speedup over per-shot tableau simulation on rotated surface-code memory under coherent R_Z noise as distance increases from 5 to 35.
watch_item: Exact non-Pauli simulation can still be computationally demanding, so performance likely depends on circuit structure, noise model, and how much equivalent-site reuse is available.
paper_title: Scalable Exact Non-Pauli Noise Simulation for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Circuits
